question.text: A light of wavelength <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3000</mn><mo> </mo><mover><mtext>A</mtext><mi>o</mi></mover></math> falls on a metal surface. Ejected <math><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo></mrow></msup></math> is further accelerated by a potential difference of <math><mi mathvariant="normal"></mi><mn>2</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> , then final K.E of the <math><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo></mrow></msup></math> is found to be <math><mn>8</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>19</mn></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></math> . If threshold energy for the metal surface is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mtext mathvariant="normal">'</mtext><msup><mtext mathvariant="normal">ϕ</mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">'</mi></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> . Then find the numerical value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">ϕ</mi></math>

solution.text:
KE final  =  E photon  +  E potential  −ϕ
where ϕ = threshold energy for metal surface
E photon  =  hc λ  =  6.6× 10 −34 ×3× 10 8 3000× 10 −10
≃6.6× 10 −19 J=4.12 eV
E potential  = 2 eV
KE final = 8× 10 −19 J 1.6× 10 −19 J =5 eV
Hence, ϕ=(4.12+2−5) eV=1.125 eV
Numerical value = 8×1.125=9
